title: AI APIs and Integrations
answer: Endpoints, SDKs, authentication, rate limits, pricing, uptime, and changelogs for every public AI API.

reading.body:
The API layer of AI is catalogued unevenly: 458 pricing entries against 18 directory entries and 13 status pages.

The counts describe how much is known about each layer, not how large each layer is. Pricing is the most documented surface, which fits a market where every provider publishes a rate card and every buyer needs one. Endpoints, SDKs, and authentication are catalogued for only 18 APIs, and reliability history for 13. Those are the numbers a developer actually needs before integrating, and they are the thinnest part of the record.

The one place the data reaches past the API surface is model serving: 112 providers that run the inference behind model APIs, each with a headquarters country and datacenter regions. That is the link between an endpoint and a building. An API call resolves to a datacenter in a named region, owned by a named company, drawing power somewhere. The catalogue records the region and the operator but nothing about the power or the capacity behind them.

What this does not cover: no list of the APIs themselves, no uptime figures, no prices, no dates beyond the build and verification stamps. The counts say how many entries exist in each child section, not what any of them contain. A reader should treat this as an index of an index, useful for knowing which questions have answers collected and which do not.
